# Spanish Damas Library

Python library implementing **Spanish Damas (Checkers)** rules with full move validation and SVG rendering.

![Demo GIF](https://www.googleapis.com/download/storage/v1/b/kaggle-user-content/o/inbox%2F7234856%2F9d74ef576673f7ae8eeb0329d9da3a31%2Fdamas_game_v2.gif?generation=1771028919735634&alt=media)

## Features
- Spanish checkers rules
- Move validation and capture logic
- SVG board rendering
- Example Jupyter notebook included

## Installation

Clone the repository:

```python
# Install the wheel
!pip install /kaggle/input/models/youneseloiarm/damas-library-001/other/default/1/damas-package/dist/damas-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl

# Test the import
from damas import *

# If your script has functions, you can test them
# For example, if your script has a function named 'process_data':
# result = damas.process_data(...)

print("✓ damas successfully imported as a library!")
```

models.description:
MedGemma 4B-IT (google/medgemma-4b-it) quantized for mobile edge deployment.

Converted from HuggingFace Safetensors to GGUF format using llama.cpp's 
conversion pipeline, then quantized to Q4_K_S (4-bit k-quant with selective 
higher precision for attention layers).

Q4_K_S was chosen over simpler Q4_0 because k-quants maintain higher fidelity 
on domain-specific medical text which is critical for clinical reasoning quality.

Specs:
- Original size: 8.6 GB (FP16)
- Quantized size: 2.2 GB (74% reduction)
- Format: GGUF Q4_K_S
- Inference: llama.cpp (CPU)
- On-device speed: 32.8 tok/s prompt processing, 7.8 tok/s generation
- Hardware tested: Snapdragon 8s Gen 3 (Realme GT Neo 6, 12 GB RAM)
models.title: medgemma-4b-q4_k_s.gguf

models.author: Sultan Umar
models.description:
BiomedCLIP vision encoder (microsoft/BiomedCLIP-PubMedBERT_256-vit_base_patch16_224) 
quantized for mobile edge deployment.

Exported from PyTorch to ONNX (opset 17), then quantized using dynamic INT8 
quantization. Dynamic quantization was chosen because it requires no calibration 
dataset and achieves near-lossless accuracy on embedding tasks.

Specs:
- Original size: 329 MB (FP32)
- Quantized size: 84 MB (74% reduction)
- Format: ONNX INT8
- Runtime: ONNX Runtime Mobile 1.19.0
- Inference speed: 114 ms/image average (validated across 400 images)
- Embedding fidelity: 0.9991 cosine similarity vs FP32
- Output: 512-dimensional L2-normalized embeddings

Evaluated on 400 chest X-rays (COVID-19 Radiography Database):
- Top-5 clinical accuracy: 98.8% (395/400)
- Top-3 clinical accuracy: 87.5% (350/400)
models.title: biomedclip_vision_int8.onnx

models.description:
## Model Overview
This model predicts the probability of heart disease from structured
clinical data such as age, blood pressure, cholesterol, and ECG features.

## Training Details
- Algorithm: CatBoostClassifier
- CV: Stratified 5-Fold
- Metric: ROC-AUC
- CV Score: ~0.955

## Input Features
See `model_features.json` for full feature list.

## Usage Example
```python
from catboost import CatBoostClassifier

model = CatBoostClassifier()
model.load_model("catboost_heart_disease_model.cbm")

preds = model.predict_proba(X_new)[:, 1]

### Load the model
```python
from catboost import CatBoostClassifier
import json
import os

MODEL_DIR = "${PATH}"
MODEL_FILE = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "catboost_heart_disease_model.cbm")
FEATURE_FILE = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "model_features.json")

model = CatBoostClassifier()
model.load_model(MODEL_FILE)

with open(FEATURE_FILE, "r") as f:
    feature_info = json.load(f)
